gaps.sentence: He was born in ___ Netherlands, not in Belgium.
gaps.explanation: Country names that are plural or contain 'Kingdom/Republic/States' take 'the': the Netherlands.

gaps.sentence: It was ___ best film of the decade by common consent.
My uncle is ___ university lecturer and a painter in his free time.
gaps.explanation: 'A university lecturer' (the u sounds like /juː/); the second gap is also 'an artist'.

gaps.sentence: They moved to ___ coastal town an hour south of the capital.
gaps.explanation: A coastal town — first mention of one of many.

gaps.sentence: They organized ___ charity concert for flood victims.
gaps.explanation: 'A charity concert' — one of many possible concerts, first mention.

gaps.sentence: ___ problem is that people don't recycle enough.
gaps.explanation: The problem (the one we are discussing); people in general takes no article.

gaps.sentence: The charity provides ___ shelter for homeless families in winter.
gaps.explanation: 'Shelter' is uncountable and general here, so no article is used.

gaps.sentence: ___ sun sets much later in summer.
gaps.explanation: 'The sun' — there is only one, so the definite article is used.
